fatal_errors: The proposed HfMoTaTiZr-Cr alloying strategy does not reconstruct the target method: modulus/VEC/density screening of 38,326 Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W compositions.
The claimed increase in Ti and Zr is contradicted by E1: their concentrations decrease from 8.1 to 7.7 at.% and from 15.4 to 14.7 at.%, respectively.
The predicted 3–5% density reduction is unsupported by the cited evidence and is not established by the reported compositional change.
The proposed Laves-phase mediator conflicts with the target result, which intentionally retained a single-phase BCC structure.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad goal of combining strength, ductility, and reduced density in an RHEA, and E1 gives partial support for Cr-induced Laves-phase formation and an approximately 208 MPa yield-strength increase in HfMoTaTiZr. It is nevertheless a different alloy system and design concept, with no reconstruction of the target composition-screening method, selected Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 composition, VEC-controlled dislocation-mobility mechanism, or measured 35.7% compressive fracture strain. Its paired-alloy compression, microscopy, diffraction, and density experiment would be discriminating, but major claims concerning increased Ti/Zr, density reduction, crack deflection, and ductility are not adequately supported by the supplied evidence; E2 is largely irrelevant.
